title: Crisp Churros with Dark Chocolate Sauce
summary: Crisp, ridged churros piped from a simple cooked dough and fried golden, served with a glossy cinnamon-scented dark chocolate sauce.
equipment: stand mixer with paddle (or wooden spoon)
piping bag with 1.5 cm closed star nozzle
baking tray lined with oiled baking paper
large heavy pan or casserole, at least 24 cm wide
wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

ingredients.note: check the label; many contain soya lecithin or traces of milk

steps.title: Cook the dough
steps.text: Put the water, butter, sugar, vanilla and salt in the large saucepan and bring to the boil. Take it off the heat, add all the flour in one go and stir vigorously until there are no dry patches. Boiling water gelatinises the starch, which gives churros their crisp shell and soft middle.

steps.title: Beat in the eggs
steps.text: Beat the dough on low for 1 min to let some heat escape, then add the eggs and beat on medium for about 1 min until smooth and glossy.

steps.title: Pipe and chill
steps.text: Spoon the warm dough into the piping bag and pipe 18 lengths of 15 cm onto the oiled paper, cutting each off with scissors. Chill them uncovered for 15-60 min; firm dough keeps its sharp ridges in the oil and is far easier to handle.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Warm the 90 g sugar, milk and cinnamon in the medium pan over medium-low heat, whisking, for about 5 min until the sugar dissolves and small bubbles appear at the edge. Turn the heat to low and whisk in the cocoa until smooth. Off the heat, add the chopped chocolate, leave it for 3 min, then whisk in the butter and vanilla until glossy.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Add oil to the heavy pan to a depth of about 4 cm, keeping it below half full, and heat to 190 °C.

steps.title: Fry until crisp
steps.text: Lower in 6 churros and fry for about 6 min, turning occasionally, with the oil kept between 180 and 190 °C. They are done when deep golden brown and crisp all over; drain them on the rack and fry the rest the same way.

steps.title: Serve hot
steps.text: Pile 3 churros onto each plate and serve straight away with the warm chocolate sauce for dipping.

tips: The most common mistake is frying straight from the bag without chilling; soft dough loses its ridges and can burst in the oil.
Use a closed star nozzle: the ridges add crunch and help the churros cook evenly.
Rewarm the sauce gently over low heat, stirring, if it thickens while you fry.
Choose a dark chocolate whose label you have checked for milk and soya if serving guests with allergies.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Churros are best eaten within an hour of frying; re-crisp leftovers in a 200 °C oven for 5 min. The chocolate sauce keeps covered in the fridge for up to 1 week; rewarm gently until pourable.
